question: What do we call the swelling that happens when fluid gets trapped in body tissues?
explanation: Spot on! Oedema is just the clinical word for when excess fluid builds up in the spaces between your body tissues, causing that puffy look. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h1)

question: Which tiny blood vessels are mainly responsible for leaking fluid into the tissues when oedema starts?
explanation: You've got it! Capillaries are the microscopic vessels where fluid normally slips back and forth between blood and tissue. When things go wrong, they leak extra fluid. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h1)

question: Which blood protein acts like a sponge to hold fluid inside the blood vessels?
explanation: Great job! Albumin creates what we call oncotic pressure—think of it as a magnet pulling fluid back into the bloodstream so it doesn't leak out into the tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h2)

question: Why does liver disease often lead to body swelling and fluid buildup?

options.A: The liver fails to destroy excess red blood cells.
options.B: The liver blocks the main lymphatic channels in the abdomen.
options.C: The liver stops producing enough blood proteins to maintain oncotic pressure.
options.D: Damaged liver cells pump too much salt directly into the bloodstream.

explanation: Exactly! The liver is our protein factory. When it's sick, it can't make enough albumin, meaning fluid escapes the blood vessels easily and causes swelling. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h2)

question: What is the term for severe, widespread swelling that affects the entire body?
explanation: Spot on! Anasarca describes heavy, generalized fluid overload where the whole body looks and feels swollen. You'll often see this in very advanced systemic illness. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h3)

question: If a patient has sudden swelling in just ONE lower leg, what is the most likely cause?

options.A: End-stage renal failure affecting total body fluid balance
options.B: Severe protein malnutrition lowering overall blood albumin
options.C: A deep vein thrombosis blocking blood return from that limb
options.D: Chronic congestive heart failure reducing cardiac output

explanation: Correct! A blood clot (DVT) in one leg blocks the highway for returning blood, causing fluid to back up right there, unlike whole-body causes like kidney or heart failure. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h3)

question: How do nurses properly check for pitting oedema at the bedside?

options.A: Measuring the circumference of the limb with a flexible tape measure
options.B: Squeezing the muscle belly firmly to test for deep pain reflexes
options.C: Pressing a finger firmly against the swollen skin over a bony area for a few seconds
options.D: Applying a cold pack to see how fast the skin temperature drops

explanation: You got it! Pressing firmly over a bone (like the shin) pushes the fluid aside momentarily. If an indent stays behind, that's a positive 'pit'! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h4)

question: What is the main difference between pitting and non-pitting oedema?

options.A: Pitting oedema only occurs on the face, while non-pitting oedema only affects the feet.
options.B: Pitting oedema leaves an indentation after pressure, while non-pitting oedema does not.
options.C: Pitting oedema is always painless, whereas non-pitting oedema causes severe sharp pain.
options.D: Pitting oedema disappears with rest, while non-pitting oedema requires surgery.

explanation: Spot on! It's all in the name. Pitting leaves a little thumbprint depression because the fluid shifts easily, whereas non-pitting (often linked to lymphatic issues) stays firm. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h4)

question: Which group of medications helps the body get rid of extra fluid through urine?
explanation: Correct! Diuretics (often called water pills) trick the kidneys into flushing out extra salt and water, which brings the swelling down. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h5)

question: A patient has swollen ankles. How should you advise them to position their legs when resting?

options.A: Dangling freely off the edge of the bed
options.B: Crossed tightly at the knees for stability
options.C: Flat on the floor while sitting in a chair
options.D: Elevated above the level of the heart

explanation: You've got this! Gravity is our helper here. Raising the legs higher than the heart lets trapped fluid flow smoothly back into circulation. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h5)

question: Why are people with long-term leg swelling at higher risk for skin infections like cellulitis?

options.A: Swollen legs attract insects that transmit bacterial infections.
options.B: Increased blood flow carries too many white blood cells to the skin.
options.C: Fluid buildup inside the tissues directly manufactures harmful bacteria.
options.D: Stretched, fragile skin easily develops cracks that let bacteria enter.

explanation: Exactly! When skin is constantly stretched out by fluid, it gets dry, thin, and fragile. Tiny cracks form easily, giving bacteria an easy doorway in. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a good self-care practice for managing long-term leg swelling?

options.A: Wearing tight, restrictive garters to keep the swelling squeezed down
options.B: Elevating the legs periodically throughout the day
options.C: Following a reduced-sodium diet as prescribed by the doctor
options.D: Inspecting the lower legs daily for any skin breaks or redness

explanation: Spot on! Avoid tight bands or restrictive garters because they actually choke off circulation and make fluid pooling worse. Proper medical compression stockings should be used instead! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h6)
